questions.q: What are rights, and why are they important for individuals?

answer.text: A right is a reasonable claim of a person, recognised by society and sanctioned by law, which is necessary for living a life of dignity. Rights are claims we make on ourselves, on other people and on the state, and they are justified because they help human beings develop their full potential.

Every right carries a corresponding duty. My right to life places on others the duty not to harm me, and my right to liberty requires others to respect my freedom. In this way rights and duties are closely linked.

Rights are important because they protect individuals from the misuse of power, especially by the state. They guarantee the basic conditions, political, economic and cultural, needed for a decent life, and they set limits on what governments may do while placing obligations on them to protect citizens.

answer: Thus rights are essential safeguards of human dignity and freedom.

questions.q: What is the relationship between rights and duties in a society?

answer.text: are closely linked, for the rights of one person imply duties on others and on the state.

list: My right to life places a duty on others not to harm me and on the state to protect me
Rights can be enjoyed only if others respect them, which is their duty
Those who claim rights must respect the equal rights of others
They have a duty to use their rights responsibly and to contribute to the common good, so rights and duties go together

questions.q: What are human rights, and why are they claimed to be universal?

answer.text: are the basic rights that belong to every person simply because they are human, regardless of nationality, race, sex or religion.

list: They include the rights to life, liberty, dignity and equality before the law
They are set out in documents like the Universal Declaration of Human Rights

answer.lead: They are said to be universal.
answer.text: They apply to all people everywhere.

list: They are not granted by any government but are inherent in being human, so no state may rightly deny them
This universality is used to defend people against oppression anywhere in the world
